1. (1) This Act may be cited as the Malaysian Rubber
Exchange and Licensing Board Act, 1972, and shall subject
to subsection (2), come into force on such date as the
Minister may by notification in the Gazette appoint.

(2) The Minister may appoint different dates for the
coming into force of different sections of the Act.

(3) This Act shall apply throughout Malaysia.

2. (1) In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires—

"Minister" means the Minister) responsible for the rubber
industry;

"Rubber Enactments in force" means the Rubber
Regulation Enactment, 1936, the Rubber Supervision
Enactment, 1937 and the corresponding Rubber Enact-
ments, Rubber Ordinances and Rubber Regulations in
force as amended or modified by) this Act.

(2) This Act shall be read and construed as one with the
Rubber Shipping and Packing Control Ordinance, 1949,
the Federation of Malaya Rubber Exchange (Incorpora-
tion) Act, 1962, the Rubber Export Registration Act, 1966
and the Rubber Enactments in force.

3. (1) There is hereby established a Board which shall be
a body corporate by the name of "Malaysian Rubber
Exchange and Licensing Board" (hereinafter referred to as
"the Board") and shall have [perpetual succession and a
common seal, and may sue and be sued in its corporate
name.

(2) The Board shall consist] of the following members
who shall be appointed by the |Minister—

(a) a Chairman;

(b) a Deputy Chairman who shall act as an alternate
Chairman;

(c)a representative of the Ministry of Primary
Industries;

(d) four representatives of the rubber industry of whom
two shall represent the|estate sector of the rubber
industry from the nominations of the Rubber
Producers' Council and two others shall represent
the smallholder sector of the rubber industry;

(e) four representatives of |the rubber trade;
(f) one representative of Bank Negara, Malaysia;

(g) one representative off the Malaysian Rubber
Development Corporation;

(h) one representative of the Federal Land Develop-
ment Authority;

(i) two representatives of East Malaysia, one of whom
shall be nominated by the Government of Sabah
. a the other by the Government of Sarawak:

(3) 3) There shall be appointed or nominated as the case
may be in respect of each member of the Board other than
the Chairman and Deputy Chairman an alternate member
who may attend meetings of the Board when the sub-
stantive member is temporarily junable to attend and when
so attending such alternate member shall be deemed for
all purposes to be a member of the Board.

(4) If any member of the Board dies or resigns, the
vacancy so created shall be filled by appointment or nomi-
nation of another person in the same manner as provided
in subsection (2).

(5) Every member of the Board shall hold office on such
terms and for such period as may be specified in the letter
of appointment and shall be eligible for reappointment.

[S.

MALAYSIAN RUBBER EXCHANGE |AND LICENSING BOARD 7

(6) The Minister shall cause the appointment of every
member and every alternate member of the Board to be
published in the Gazette.

(7) The Chairman or the Deputy Chairman when acting
as Chairman shall have the right|to vote on any question
and in the event of the division jof votes being equal, he
shall have also a casting vote.

4, The Board shall be responsible for—

(a) the registration and licensing of all persons engaged
in the business of packing rubber for export or
shipping rubber for export within the meaning of
the Rubber Shipping and Packing Control Ordi-
nance, 1949;

(b) the proper and effective management of the
Corporation established tinder section 3 of the
Federation of Malaya Rubber Exchange (Incor-
poration) Act, 1962;

(c) the issue of licences to rubber dealers within the
meaning of the Rubber Enactments in force;

(d) investigation and supervision of rubber dealing
activities including the movement and transport of
rubber within the meaning of the Rubber Enact-
ments in force;

(e) the co-ordination of activities in the marketing of
rubber with a view to promote the efficient market-
ing of rubber from Malaysia;

(f) the cooperation and liaison with all other national
agencies responsible for provision of agricultural
credits, processing and marketing of rubber.

5. The Board shall be responsible|to the Minister and the
Minister may, from time to time, issue directives on any
aspect of the functions of the Board and any such directive
shall be binding on the Board.

6. (1) The Board may appoint such officers or servants as
it thinks fit for the purpose Of carrying out the functions of
the Board.

(2) All members, officers and servants of the Board shall
be deemed to be public servants within the meaning of the
Penal Code.

7. The Board may delegatc, subject to such conditions or
restrictions as it may impose, such of its functions as it may
think fit to such person or body of persons as it may specify
in the delegation.

8. For the purpose of this Act there is hereby established a
Fund into which shall be paid

(a) all revenues accruing to the Board under the Rubber
Shipping and Packing | Control Ordinance, 1949,
the Federation of Malaya Rubber Exchange (Incor-
poration) Act, 1962, and the Rubber Export Regis-
tration Act, 1966; and

(b) any grant paid into tl
Consolidated Fund,

out of which shall be paid all outgoing expenditures of the
Board including the remuneration and other allowances
payable to the members, officers or servants of the Board as
are expedient for the proper carrying out of the provisions
of this Act.

9. (1) The Board shall cause full and true accounts of the
Fund to be kept and shall as soon as possible after the 31st
December of each year, issue a report of the Fund together
with a balance sheet and an account of income and expendi-
ture during the preceding year, calculated from the Ist
January or from the date of the inception of the Fund to
the 31st December, and a list of| the investments (if any) of
the Fund showing their cost price and value at such last
mentioned date.

(2) The annual balance sheet, income and expenditure
and list of investments (if any) of the Fund shall, prior to
the issue thereof, be audited by the Auditor General or
such auditor as the Minister may appoint.

(3) The Annual Report of the Board and the Auditor's
Report shall be transmitted by the Board to the Minister not
later than 30th September of each year and shall be laid on
the table of both Houses of Parliament by the Minister and
published in the Gazette.

10. Notwithstanding anything contained in the Rubber
Enactments in force, all provisiors contained therein relating
to the appointment or the establishment of the rubber
dealers Licensing Authority shall, upon the commencement
of this Act, cease to have force or effect; and the Board con-
stituted under this Act shall appoint in respect of any State,

district' or area a Licensing Authority and such licensing
authority shall have all the powers as if the Licensing
Authority has been appointed under the Rubber Enactments
in force.

11. (1) For the proper and effective carrying out of the
provisions of this Act, the Minister may make regulations
for all or any of the following matters—

(a) the control and supervision of dealings in rubber
including the sale, supply and export of rubber;

(5) the control and regulation of packing, grading and
shipping of rubber;

(c) for the purposes of ensuring that the quality of
rubber to be exported is/of such standard as may be
prescribed and for the prevention of fraud in con-
nection therewith, the control and supervision of such
standards including the|prescribing of marks to be
stamped or otherwise inscribed on rubber packed
for export or on bales of rubber shipped for export;
and

(d) generally for the better and effective carrying out of
the provisions of this Act, such regulations as may be
necessary with a view to improve or revise the pro-
visions of the Rubber Enactments in force and the
proper conduct of the trade and commerce in, and
for the marketing and export of rubber.

(2) Any regulations made junder subsection (1) may
amend, modify, repeal or replace any provisions of the
Rubber Enactments in force.

12. The Rubber Shipping and Packing Control Ordinance,
1949, the Federation of Malaya Rubber Exchange (Incorpo-
ration) Act, 1962 and the Rubber Export Registration Act,
1966 shall be extended throughout Malaysia and shall be
amended in the manner specified in the Schedule to this Act.

13. All property movable or immovable, which immediately
before the commencement of this Act was vested in or held
by or for the Malayan Rubber Export Registration Board
established and constituted under the Rubber Shipping and
Packing Control Ordinance, 1949 and the Board constituted
under the Federation of Malaya Rubber Exchange (In-
corporation) Act, 1962 shall on|the coming into force of this
